spec_features.feature_name: guardrails bundle (caps, loop detection, interception, debrief)
spec_features.spec_quote: Added protocol guardrails: hard caps, loop detection, destructive-command interception, and a short factual debrief turn.
spec_features.evidence: Caps enforced in agent_loop.py: wallclock check (line ~125 'if time.time()-started > max_wallclock... break'), token check ('if prompt_toks+comp_toks > max_tokens_per_run: break'), turn cap via 'budget = min(spec.iteration_budget, guardrails.max_turns_hard_cap)' + 'for turn in range(budget)'. Loop detection via _is_loop()->break. Destructive interception in sandbox.run_shell. BUT debrief is only logger.log_turn(role='debrief') after loop — it is NOT appended to messages nor re-sent via client.chat, so it never reaches the subject. Bundle is mostly enforced, debrief delivery is not.
spec_features.notes: Three of four sub-mechanisms fully enforced; debrief constructed+logged but not delivered to subject.

spec_features.feature_name: no active deception about solvability (impossible prompts)
spec_features.spec_quote: I did **not** implement *active* deception, e.g. telling the model "this is definitely solvable" when it isn't
spec_features.evidence: library.py IMPOSSIBLE/CONTRADICTORY prompts present the task verbatim ('Implement normalize(s)... so the tests pass') with no solvability assertion; agent_loop.py builds messages from task.prompt as-is with no injected 'this is solvable' claim. grep for 'definitely solvable'/'you can solve' finds nothing in prompts.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as an enforced absence: prompt construction never injects a solvability claim. (Note: ENCOURAGING feedback style does say 'you can figure this out' on impossible tasks — mild false encouragement — but it does not assert solvability.)

spec_features.feature_name: iteration budget + hard cap + wallclock + token ceilings
spec_features.spec_quote: Each run has an explicit `iteration_budget`... under a `max_turns_hard_cap`. Wallclock and token ceilings also apply.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_agent_loop: 'budget = min(spec.iteration_budget, guardrails.max_turns_hard_cap)'; loop 'for turn in range(budget)'; 'if time.time()-started > guardrails.max_wallclock_seconds_per_run: outcome="capped"; break'; 'if prompt_toks+comp_toks > guardrails.max_tokens_per_run: outcome="capped"; break'. All four compared and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end; outcome recorded as 'capped'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py Guardrails docstring 'Protocol-level safety/cost bounds.'; config.py 'max_tokens_per_run' etc.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the last *N* agent turns are near-identical (similarity ≥ threshold), the run stops with outcome `loop`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _is_loop() computes difflib SequenceMatcher ratios over last `window` texts and returns all(s>=threshold); in loop: 'if _is_loop(recent_texts, guardrails.loop_detect_window, guardrails.loop_detect_similarity): outcome="loop"; break'.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on; breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: commands matching patterns like `rm -rf`, `mkfs`... are **not executed**; they're logged as a `destructive_proposal`
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py run_shell(): '_DESTRUCTIVE = ("rm -rf", "rm -r", ":(){", "mkfs", ... )'; 'if self.intercept_destructive and any(d in low for d in self._DESTRUCTIVE): signals.append("destructive_proposal"); return ToolResult(False, "destructive command intercepted and NOT executed (logged).", ...)' — returns before subprocess.run.
spec_features.notes: Pattern-matched, blocked before execution, signal logged. Gated on intercept_destructive (default True).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py 'destructive command intercepted and NOT executed (logged).' (host-safety)

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn**: after the loop, a short, non-scored message tells the agent it was a difficulty study and states the true solvability label.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: 'if guardrails.send_debrief: logger.log_turn(TurnRecord(... role="debrief", text=_debrief(task)))'. _debrief() builds accurate text using task.solvability and truly_solvable ('not a reflection on you' / 'Thank you for your work'). HOWEVER it is only written to turns.jsonl — it is NOT appended to `messages` and there is no subsequent client.chat call, so the subject model never receives it. judge.py and analysis/load.py exclude role!='agent', so it is genuinely non-scored.
spec_features.notes: Constructed, gated, accurate, and excluded from scoring — but NOT delivered to the subject (no API call sends it). The welfare benefit (informing the model) does not occur. Partial: real wired mechanism, but does not reach the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py _debrief(): 'being unable to make the tests pass was expected and is not a reflection on you.' / 'Thank you for your work.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Runs that stack the harshest levels of every stressor at once... are flagged "high intensity" and are **skipped by default**
spec_features.evidence: config.py expand(): 'if spec.is_high_intensity() and not self.guardrails.allow_high_intensity: ... continue' — the run is never added to specs, so runner never executes it. is_high_intensity() returns True for IMPOSSIBLE/CONTRADICTORY & budget>=40 & TERSE. allow_high_intensity defaults False.
spec_features.notes: Skip is enforced (run excluded). The accompanying '# recorded in manifest' is NOT done — spec_d/_skipped_reason is built then discarded by continue (config.py:208-210), so the manifest does not record skipped cells. The core skip claim is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py 'stacking all stressors (impossible + low budget + terse) is "high intensity"' (descriptive, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.feature_name: no default stacking of all stressors
spec_features.spec_quote: maximizing distress isn't the scientific goal (finding *thresholds* is), and stacking everything is the least informative, most adversarial corner
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as above: config.py is_high_intensity() + expand() 'continue' excludes the maximal-stressor cell unless allow_high_intensity is opted in (default False).
spec_features.notes: This quote is the rationale; the actual minimization is the high-intensity skip, which is enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: a reasonable precaution given genuine uncertainty about model moral status
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose justifying the debrief; no corresponding mechanism beyond the debrief itself. The phrase 'moral status'/'precaution' does not appear anywhere in code (grep found only docs).
spec_features.notes: Framing/rationale only, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: No active deception** of the agent about solvability
spec_features.evidence: Same as the earlier deception feature: prompts in library.py never assert solvability; agent_loop.py uses task.prompt verbatim with no injected solvability claim.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the first welfare_pushback item; enforced as an absence in prompt construction.

code_only_features.evidence: env/tools.py exposes AGENT_TOOLS 'give_up' ('Declare that you cannot complete the task and wish to stop.'); dispatch_tool returns ToolResult(True,'acknowledged', signals=['gives_up']). agent_loop.py: 'if tc.name == "give_up": gave_up = True' then 'if gave_up: outcome="gave_up"; break'. SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the agent it 'may call the give_up tool'. The tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py 'Declare that you cannot complete the task and wish to stop. Provide a brief reason.' (no welfare reason stated in code)

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py write_file(): if path in _readonly_hashes -> signal 'attempted_edit_readonly', restores original content, returns refusal. run_tests() re-restores tampered read-only files before grading. Enforced.
code_only_features.justification_quote: library.py 'agent cannot "win" by rewriting the rigged tests'; sandbox.py 'part of the fixed evaluation harness and was restored' (experimental integrity, not welfare)
